average-qps.why: 100,000,000 × 20 = 2 billion requests a day; ÷ 86,400 ≈ 23,148 per second.

peak-qps.why: Peak = average × stated peak factor: 23,148 × 3 ≈ 69,444. The factor is an assumption you state, not a number you invent silently.

yearly-storage.why: 10 GB × 365 = 3,650 GB = 3.65 TB. Add replication and indexes on top in a real estimate.

cache-size.why: 1,000,000 × 2,000 bytes = 2,000,000,000 bytes = 2 GB, before per-entry overhead.

uploads-per-second.why: 5,000,000 ÷ 86,400 ≈ 58 per second on average; peaks will be higher.

state-assumptions.why: Estimates are only as good as their assumptions. Saying 'assuming 3× at peak' turns a guess into a reasoned, revisable number.
